title: A bake-off harness: DCLab's engine against FLAML on the same rows, holdout, folds and metric, its rule fixed before the run
request: Package 34.5 of the phase-10 plan: compare DCLab's engine as it is with FLAML (owner-approved pip install) on the 10 UCI sets, Telco and the expansion samples, same splits, metric and time budget; holdout score with interval, minutes and peak memory per dataset; stored as an evidence campaign; the rule deciding 34.8 fixed before the run. Small budgets on the 8 GB Air.
spec: dclab_rnd/bakeoff.py and make bakeoff. Each dataset becomes a studio project from its sample and the R&D's solution (saved through the graph's set_solution). The engine runs its five stages in a child process with no model offered; its holdout predictions are taken from the final stage's one holdout fit and must reproduce its record. FLAML 2.7.0 runs in another process on engine.prepare's bundle: the engine's raw tabular columns, the engine's training folds as a fixed splitter, the same metric, a 300 s budget, predicting the holdout once. A compare step checks the same holdout rows, labels, groups, folds and columns, then each engine's bootstrap interval and a paired bootstrap of the difference. The rule, the protocol, FLAML's settings and version and the hash of the code that applies them are frozen in the manifest before the first run; results are written once.
plan: read the plan, the expansion datasets and the studio engine
choose how each engine gets the same split
install FLAML and read how it splits
write the harness, the rule and the freeze
test on a tiny grouped table through the real orchestration
review before the real run (results are written once)
run the bake-off when the machine is free (owner's call)

decisions.decision: Run the studio engine (all five stages) rather than the expansion runner's campaign
decisions.why: the expansion runner loads only its four datasets; the studio engine is the engine the product runs on any table, and its prepare() gives one bundle both engines can share

decisions.decision: Give FLAML the engine's own training folds as a splitter object
decisions.why: FLAML reshuffles rows for its string split types; a splitter object is used as given (no shuffle, no rare-class augment), so both search on the same folds

decisions.decision: Take the engine's holdout predictions by wrapping fit_and_predict during the final stage and check them against the record
decisions.why: the record keeps no predictions; refitting would be a second holdout read; the check proves the captured predictions are the recorded ones

decisions.decision: Each engine in its own process
decisions.why: its wall time and peak memory are its own, and a crash or the OS ending one on 8 GB does not end the campaign

decisions.decision: FLAML gets the raw tabular columns, not the engine's engineered features
decisions.why: a bake-off of engines as they are; the text dataset, where FLAML then sees no text, is reported but not judged by the rule

decisions.decision: A fixed 300 s FLAML budget, the engine's time measured
decisions.why: the engine has no time knob; the brief asks for about five minutes per engine per dataset; time never enters the rule

decisions.decision: Rule: FLAML ahead (paired 95% interval above 0) on at least a third of the judged datasets and on more than it is behind; at least 10 judged; a FLAML failure counts as behind
decisions.why: the owner's proposal made exact: paired on the same rows is stricter than two overlapping intervals, and failures and early stops cannot bend the count

change: dclab_rnd/bakeoff.py (new); tests/test_bakeoff.py (new, 14 tests); Makefile (bakeoff target); requirements/base.txt (flaml==2.7.0).

findings.defect: FLAML would have searched on its own reshuffled folds, not the engine's
findings.scenario: split_type='stratified' or 'group' makes FLAML shuffle X_train and build its own folds
findings.cause: FLAML's prepare_data shuffles for uniform and stratified split types
findings.fix: pass the engine's bundle.cv_splits as a splitter object with shuffle=False; auto_augment off so no rare row is duplicated
findings.impact: the two engines would have been chosen on different folds

findings.defect: the text dataset counted in the rule while FLAML saw no text
findings.scenario: ecommerce_clothing_reviews: FLAML gets 4 raw columns, the engine the text too; one dataset can flip a 5-of-14 rule
findings.cause: the arm uses raw tabular columns; 34.8 would give FLAML the recipe's features
findings.fix: the rule names it 'not judged' and decide() leaves it out
findings.impact: the rule would measure the wrong thing on that dataset

findings.defect: one dataset's exception stopped the whole campaign on every rerun
findings.scenario: a download or hash failure, or compare's refusal of different splits, raised out of run()
findings.cause: no try/except around a dataset's prepare, compare and report
findings.fix: each dataset in _run_dataset inside a handler that writes dataset.failed.json and goes on

findings.defect: a DCLab retry after a kill or timeout could never succeed
findings.scenario: the OS ends the child during models: the project stays marked running; a rerun's data stage is refused by the graph ('nothing else running'); after a final stage the holdout counts as used
findings.cause: a retry reused the same project
findings.fix: every DCLab retry (and a resume where the engine never finished) starts on a fresh project; FLAML's outputs go with it
findings.impact: a dataset hit by memory pressure on 8 GB would fail forever

findings.defect: the freeze pinned the rule's words, not the code and settings that apply it
findings.scenario: edit decide() or upgrade FLAML between datasets: the run resumes silently
findings.cause: only RULE and the protocol's prose were hashed
findings.fix: the protocol holds FLAML's settings, metric map and version, the draws and seed, and the sha256 of the source of decide, paired_bootstrap, compare, the arms and the column choice
findings.impact: the rule could change after the first result without anyone seeing

findings.defect: a decision could be written early, and failures left the denominator
findings.scenario: report --final wrote the permanent decision once any 10 datasets finished; an arm failure silently left the count
findings.cause: no rule for failures or an early stop
findings.fix: --final only when every dataset not compared failed after its retry; a FLAML failure counts as behind, a DCLab-only failure is left out and listed
findings.impact: stopping on a good score, or FLAML failures favouring FLAML

findings.defect: the Solution was saved without the workflow graph's check and log
findings.cause: a shortcut past the validator other harnesses use
findings.fix: graph.check(set_solution) and graph.log, as real_problems.py does
findings.impact: a move outside the graph's record

findings.defect: the two processes' columns and fold contents were not compared
findings.scenario: 22.9's routed decisions inside prepare could give one process other identifiers
findings.cause: compare checked rows, labels and fold sizes only
findings.fix: each engine's split record keeps the model columns and a hash of the fold indices; compare refuses a difference
findings.impact: an unseen difference in inputs between the arms

findings.defect: small leaks of the run into other systems
findings.scenario: DCLAB_DATABASE_URL in the shell would send 14 scratch projects' records to PostgreSQL; a results key 'verdict' is read elsewhere as pass or fail
findings.cause: the child's environment and the key name
findings.fix: DCLAB_DATABASE_URL blanked in the child; the keys renamed comparison and outcome; flaml pinned in requirements/base.txt
findings.impact: agent metrics would log every bake-off result as a failed evaluation

findings.defect: FLAML failed on one dataset in the full run
findings.scenario: the spambase table's column names hold characters LightGBM refuses (inside FLAML)
findings.cause: the harness handed FLAML the engine's column names as they are
findings.fix: _flaml_frame renames the columns to c0, c1, ... before FLAML sees them; the frozen protocol hash refuses a rerun under bakeoff_v1, so the fix serves a later bakeoff_v2
findings.impact: spambase counted as FLAML behind by the rule's failure clause; the decision does not depend on it
alternatives: edit the frozen campaign (refused: a changed protocol is a new campaign)
findings.open: a bakeoff_v2 with the fix and AutoGluon on the M1 Max

findings.defect: the campaign report hid a failure and a dataset the rule did not judge
findings.scenario: spambase, where FLAML failed, had no row; the text dataset showed 'flaml behind' though the rule left it out
findings.cause: the report listed only datasets with a result file and printed each comparison as measured
findings.fix: a row for each failure with how the rule counted it; a dataset the rule did not judge says so
findings.impact: a reader could count the wrong datasets behind

measurements.name: the harness on a tiny grouped table (420 rows, 30 stores), both engines, FLAML 3 s
measurements.gate: same holdout rows, labels, folds and columns; FLAML fitted on training rows only and predicting the holdout once; the engine's captured predictions reproduce its record; intervals around both scores
measurements.next: the full bake-off (make bakeoff ARGS="run --yes") when the owner is back and the machine is free
limits: a tiny invented table; the real run is not done

measurements.name: the full bake-off, 14 datasets (bakeoff_v1), on an 8 GB MacBook Air
measurements.gate: 34.8 goes ahead when FLAML is clearly ahead (paired 95% interval above 0) on at least a third of the datasets both engines finished
measurements.result: 13 judged (the text dataset not judged: FLAML sees no text); FLAML clearly ahead on 1 (bank marketing, +0.018), behind on 3 (letter, wine; spambase by a harness failure), no clear difference on 9; 5 were needed: no go for 34.8
measurements.next: 34.8 not built; the engine's own search (34.7) measured instead
limits: a five-minute FLAML budget on an 8 GB Air
FLAML saw the raw columns, not the engine's features

outcome: The bake-off harness is built, reviewed and tested; the rule that decides 34.8 is in code and will be frozen into the manifest by the first run. The run itself (14 datasets, about 2 to 3 hours) waits for the owner. The run (2026-10-25) said no go for 34.8: FLAML clearly ahead on 1 of 13 datasets where 5 were needed; FLAML used its whole five-minute budget on each dataset, while the engine needed under a minute on 8 of 13.
lessons: Before comparing two engines, make them read the same folds, not just the same holdout: an AutoML library reshuffles unless given a splitter object.
Freeze the code that applies a rule, not only its words.
On an 8 GB machine a retry must start clean: a killed run leaves state that blocks the next one.
A rule fixed before the run decides even when a harness bug lands in the results: count the failure both ways and say whether the decision moves; here it did not.
risks: FLAML sees the engine's raw columns, not its engineered features: a no-go would not prove FLAML as a family behind the recipe is useless
one holdout per dataset: wide intervals on small sets (heart disease, 61 rows) make 'ahead' hard to reach
the fraud sample keeps the latest 20,000 rows: few positives in the holdout
